title: Quantized op misrouting triggered repeated executor crash loop; post-incident stabilization and observability work
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: During a scheduled autoscaling event for a high-traffic customer, a recent quantized-kernel routing heuristic incorrectly selected an unsupported fused attention op for an int8 model variant. The selection led to an executor crash loop on a subset of pods; autoscaler repeatedly spun up new instances which immediately failed, causing sustained degradation for that customer and triggering failover to a higher-cost fallback pool. This ticket captures the incident summary, immediate mitigations, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: At 2026-03-01 22:18 UTC a Canary autoscale triggered creation of 16 new q8 worker pods. 5 pods entered crash loops within 90s due to 'unsupported-op' failure in the int8 fused-attention kernel path. Error signatures showed a serialization mismatch between compiled kernels and runtime op fingerprinting after a recent kernel selector change. The autoscaler continued to provision pods and traffic was routed to degraded instances; downstream failover did not kick in cleanly causing 27 minutes of elevated latency and partial request loss for the affected customer. No customer data exposure occurred.
timeline: 2026-03-01 22:18 UTC: Autoscale event starts for customer cluster A
2026-03-01 22:19 UTC: First crashloop observed on q8-worker-05; ops team alerted by SLO pager
2026-03-01 22:22 UTC: Crash signature aggregated; initial rollback attempted but autoscaler continued to create new nodes
2026-03-01 22:34 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied: block q8 kernel selector for the affected model family; traffic drained to dedicated fallback pool
2026-03-01 22:45 UTC: Customer-facing latency and error rates return to baseline after manual traffic gating
2026-03-01 23:10 UTC: Incident declared resolved; postmortem work scheduled
root_cause: A recent heuristic change in the kernel selection path allowed an int8 model to be paired with a fused-attention kernel variant that had not been fingerprinted against our int8 op substrate. The mismatch created an unsupported opcode sequence at runtime. Contributing factors: 1) unit tests for kernel compatibility did not include cross-quantization op fingerprints, 2) canary autoscale flow lacked a pre-attach compatibility check, and 3) observability did not surface preflight kernel compatibility failures with high enough signal to trigger automated fallback before pod creation.
mitigations: Immediate: Block q8 fused-attention kernel variant from selector for affected model family (applied 2026-03-01 22:34 UTC)
Immediate: Route affected customer to verified fallback pool for 48 hours
Short-term: Add pre-attach kernel compatibility probe in autoscaler flow to validate chosen kernel against runtime op fingerprinting
Short-term: Increase log level and add metric 'kernel_compatibility_failure_count' with alert threshold 1 to oncall channel
Monitoring: Add histogram of 'time_to_detect_kernel_mismatch' to debug latency in detection path
action_items: Marco Hernandez; due 2026-03-21; Implement pre-attach kernel-compatibility probe in autoscaler that runs lightweight op-fingerprint check before provisioning a new pod
Olga Petrov; due 2026-03-18; Expand kernel fingerprint unit tests to include cross-quantization matrix (int4/int8/fp16) for top 20 customer models
Jun Park; due 2026-03-25; Add a canary gating step: first N requests on new pods are validated against a small test prompt and failures trigger immediate pod quarantine and autoscaler backoff
SRE Team; due 2026-03-16; Create an automated rollback policy in autoscaler: if crashloops > 1 within 2 minutes, stop provisioning new nodes and circuit-breaker to fallback pool
DX/Observability; due 2026-03-14; Add 'kernel_compatibility_failure_count' metric and alert; add dashboard tile summarizing kernel selector decisions per model family
Security; due 2026-03-28; Review any KMS/HSM interactions touched by autoscale probes (note: no customer data was exposed)
followups: Introduce a 'kernel signature registry' RFC for storing certified kernel fingerprints per model
Perform a 1-week canary campaign for the new autoscaler probe against low-traffic customers before broad rollout
Evaluate adding a 'safe-mode' runtime that only selects conservative kernels for first-10-minutes after node spinup
Incorporate quantization-aware fuzz tests into CI to exercise uncommon op sequences
runbook_changes: Add step: On kernel compatibility failure, immediately mark node Unschedulable and notify SRE to block autoscaler from creating nodes for that model family
Add playbook entry: How to temporarily pin kernel selector by model tag and how to rehydrate nodes from fallback pool
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/229 - emergency block list for kernel selectors
notes: Customer impacted is on dedicated capacity with reserved pool; cost of fallback routing was absorbed by SLA credit per contract
This incident differs from prior quantization regressions: failure mode was mismatched kernel fingerprint rather than numeric accuracy drift
Consider aligning kernel selector changes with a formal canary window and a preflight compatibility gate in CI
Ops observed that autoscaler default concurrency ramp caused repeated reprovisioning; will evaluate backoff tuning
